title: Injectivity of canonical enveloping map
statement: Let $K$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional nonzero associative unital central simple $K$-algebra. The canonical unital $K$-algebra homomorphism $A \otimes_K A^{\mathrm{op}} \to \operatorname{End}_K(A)$, sending $a \otimes b^{\mathrm{op}}$ to the linear map $v \mapsto avb$, is injective.

source.place: Tag 074I, Lemma 11.4.10, injectivity argument; tensor simplicity in Tag 074G, Lemma 11.4.8

proof.text: The opposite algebra is finite-dimensional central simple. By the tensor simplicity result of Stacks Tag 074G, the enveloping algebra A tensor A^op is simple. The kernel of its unital homomorphism to End_K(A) is a two-sided ideal, hence either zero or the whole algebra. It is not the whole algebra because one maps to the identity endomorphism, which is nonzero: its value at one is one in the nonzero algebra A. The kernel is therefore zero; subtracting two elements with equal image gives their equality. This argument proves injectivity without the dimension-comparison step of the parent node.

proof_origin.place: Tag 074I, Lemma 11.4.10, injectivity argument; tensor simplicity in Tag 074G, Lemma 11.4.8
